# P28.3 — Contradictions & count reconciliation surfaced (Round 6 / DEPTH.3)

**Spec:** `docs/tickets/P28.3__contradictions-reconciliation.md` · **ADR:** none new (ADR-099 covers the
materialize-at-scale posture) · **Base:** `devin/p28-2-sharing-relationship-network` · **Deferral:**
D-R6.3-CONTRADICTIONS (opened; live-over-hosted).

## Summary

Materialises the first-class, VISIBLE §31 **contradiction object** from real claims over the resolved
spine — SIG's signature: disagreement is data, not noise. The write path was genuinely missing: the
`contradiction` table had never held a row (launch computed contradictions on read,
`api.store_pg._compute_on_read`, ADR-092). This ticket adds it — **append-only, idempotent (+0), and
lifecycle-aware** — by **consuming** the §29 reconciliation (`reconcile.counts`), the §31 contradiction
entity (`reconcile.contradiction`), the model lifecycle, and the §28 resolver — never re-implementing
them (SIG-ENG-035). The 299-vs-190 count disagreement is detected and **kept VISIBLE with evidence on
both sides, never reconciled away** (§3.1). The hosted-over-`sig-pg` run is honestly deferred
(D-R6.3-CONTRADICTIONS) — no fabricated hosted count.

## What changed

- **`db/` — new sqitch change `contradiction_materialize`** (deploy/revert/verify + `sqitch.plan`): a
  nullable `input_digest` column on `contradiction` + a partial UNIQUE index
  `contradiction_input_digest_key` (mirrors `resolution_materialize` / `relationship_materialize` /
  ADR-099, `claim_content_digest` / ADR-059) so the materializer can `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO
  NOTHING`. The digest folds in the lifecycle `status`, so a lifecycle transition lands as a NEW row.
  Additive, back-compatible (nullable, no default).
- **`reconcile/materialize.py` + `reconcile materialize-contradictions --dsn`** — reads tier-0,
  belief-filtered claim groups from the spine, runs the §28 `RESOLVE` (the SAME detector
  `_compute_on_read` uses — which runs the §29.1 count-basis reconciliation), and writes an append-only,
  idempotent `contradiction` row for every genuine conflict (insert-only; no UPDATE/DELETE; re-run +0).
  Both evidence sides live in `claim_ids`. **Lifecycle-aware:** a prior OPEN contradiction the resolver
  no longer detects over the current spine is materialised as a NEW `superseded` state row via the model
  `Contradiction.supersede()` — the open row is retained in history, never deleted (SIG-RECON-021/055).
  `contradiction_row` maps ANY `reconcile.model.Contradiction`, so `reconcile.counts` (§29) and
  `reconcile.lifecycle` (§29.4) output materialises through the same writer.
  `read_materialized_contradictions` mirrors `api.store_pg._persisted_contradictions` — the real, live
  contradiction dataset the P28.5 surface refresh consumes.
- **`reconcile.materialize.read_claim_groups`** gains an optional `as_of_belief` param (mirrors
  `api.store_pg._public_claim_groups`) so an append-only retraction (a closed `sys_period`) drops a
  claim from the current belief. Default unchanged → P28.1 behaviour untouched.

## Design decisions

- **Reuse, not re-implement (SIG-ENG-035).** The detector is `reconcile.resolve.RESOLVE`; the §31 entity
  + content-derived identity is `reconcile.contradiction.materialize`; the append-only lifecycle is the
  `reconcile.model.Contradiction` transition; the §29 count reconciliation is `reconcile.counts`. The
  writer is a pure mapping over any `reconcile.model.Contradiction` — unit tests prove `reconcile_counts`
  (the canonical 299-vs-190) and `render_lifecycle_status` (procurement-vs-physical) materialise through it.
- **Mirror the compute-on-read shape.** The persisted rows are drop-in for what the surface reads:
  `read_materialized_contradictions` returns the `_persisted_contradictions` projection exactly.
- **Contradictions stay VISIBLE.** Written and read back open; a resolved-by-later-evidence finding is a
  NEW `superseded` row, never a delete/UPDATE. Nothing is silently reconciled — the point of the ticket.
- **No new ADR.** ADR-099 covers the materialize-at-scale posture; the §29/§31 semantics are consumed,
  not newly decided.
